_comment: WAVE TWO OF THE OPENGL ACTIVATION: closing the real activation boundary.
IT IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Registering the one symbol
that belongs here would strip its original PROC and then fail to link. The reason is below.
WHAT WAVE TWO IS FOR. Wave one registered InitDirectDraw, gfxPipeline::BeginGfx and
gfxPipeline::EndGfx on the claim that those three were the only callers of the DirectDraw
bring-up. That claim came from the pseudocode kit and it is wrong. A caller scan done against
the instruction bytes - over the symbol references in game.asm.pristine, and again by
disassembling midtown2.exe with capstone and matching every rel32 and every absolute dword
against the four target addresses - gives:
BeginGfx2D  0x004A9370  <- InitDirectDraw (x2), gfxPipeline::BeginGfx
BeginGfx3D  0x004A96C0  <- BeginPhase, gfxPipeline::BeginGfx
EndGfx2D    0x004AAA10  <- Main (x2), EndPhase, gfxPipeline::EndGfx
EndGfx3D    0x004AA760  <- EndPhase, gfxPipeline::EndGfx
Only BeginPhase matters. Its BeginGfx3D() call is unconditional and BeginGfx3D's first act is
lpDD->CreateSurface, which is the null dereference at BeginGfx3D+0x90 that a -gl run reports.
Main and EndPhase are safe: every COM pointer in EndGfx2D and EndGfx3D is null-tested before
use, so under -gl they run to completion and do nothing but ShowCursor, DestroyWindow and the
texture/bitmap list teardown.
SO THE ONE SYMBOL WAVE TWO WANTS IS:
?BeginPhase@@YAX_N@Z    0x00401AA0   0x330 bytes
It qualifies under the rule that governs the whole design - its original body contains no
DirectDraw or Direct3D COM at all - and the transcription in code/midtown2/agigl/
glbeginphase.cpp is written and complete. It carries exactly one conditional, at the
BeginGfx3D call site, so both arms share the entire rest of the body and the transcription is
exercised on every run rather than only under -gl. That is what makes it checkable by the same
66,068-line log diff that signed off wave one.
WHY IT IS NOT LISTED. Three of the globals BeginPhase touches cannot be named from C++:
useIME       0x006B19BC   game.asm.pristine:881874   `useIME LABEL BYTE`
audioFlags   0x006B1670   game.asm.pristine:881668   `audioFlags LABEL BYTE`
inputDevice  0x006B16F8   game.asm.pristine:881702   `inputDevice LABEL BYTE`
tools/ghidra/ExportAsm.java emits `PUBLIC <name>` only for symbols beginning with '?', so a
mangled global is linkable and an undecorated one is a module-local label. There is no PUBLIC
line above any of these three and no other spelling of them in the image. Registering
BeginPhase today strips its 0x330 bytes and the link then fails on three unresolved externals.
TO ENABLE, IN THIS ORDER:
1. Make ExportAsm.java emit PUBLIC for undecorated data labels too, and re-export/reimport.
The C++ side is already prepared: glbeginphase.cpp declares the three extern "C" and
reconciles the leading underscore with /alternatename, the same way glwin32.h reconciles
the __stdcall import decorations.
2. -DARTS_AGIGL_PHASE in tools/build.py.
3. ARTS_EXPORT void BeginPhase(bool arg1); under its mangled-name comment in
misc/freefuncs.h - asm.py works from the header markers, and a free function has no
generated header, which is the trap InitDirectDraw hit in wave one.
4. Move ?BeginPhase@@YAX_N@Z from this comment into "ported" here and into data/ported.json.
5. Run WITHOUT -gl first and diff the log. Nothing but tid values may differ.
See docs/opengl_activation.md, 'The real activation boundary'.
